title: Figma: when to use what
description: Component strategy for the Lew42 design system: two things to sync, one ladder of linkage, a few clear lines.

add.text:
Figma keeps exactly two kinds of thing in sync:

- **Values** (colour, padding, gap, radius, text size, shadow) through **variables and styles**. A **mode** is a set of values for a whole area, and it cascades to everything inside.
- **Structure** (which layers exist, their order, nesting, layout direction) through a **main component** and its instances.

Everything else (variants, properties, slots, swap, detach) is a way to let one copy **differ** from its master, and each one gives up some linkage. So the question is never "which feature?" It's: **how should this copy differ, and what am I willing to unlink?**
add.title: The short answer: two things to sync

add.text:
1. **Instance, text or image typed over.** Fully linked: master edits still arrive.
2. **+ a property** (on/off, text, icon swap). Still fully linked.
3. **Variant switch.** Linked, but to a *different* master. Variants share nothing except tokens; each one is a full copy to keep up.
4. **Slot content edited.** That **whole slot** now belongs to the copy, and master changes to that slot stop arriving. Forum reports say editing one item marks the entire slot as overridden; a test is running.
5. **Detached.** Belongs to the copy. Nothing arrives except token values.

**Rebase** = step 5 done on purpose, then *make it a new master*. You fork once, name the fork, and its copies are linked again (back to step 1).
add.title: The linkage ladder (most linked at the top)

add.text:
**Always**
1. Bind every colour, padding, gap and radius to a token, every text to a text style, and every card shadow to the `Card shadow` style.
2. **Repeat = master.** The second time you build the same arrangement, make it a master. If it repeats only here, the first one *is* the master (inline master).
3. Edit the master, not a copy. Agents: always.
4. Size copies with Fill or Hug. Never type a width on an instance (it sticks as an override).
5. Name a component set `X Set`.

**Never**
1. Never rearrange the inside of a slot for something that repeats. Make that arrangement a master first.
2. Never make a variant for a value (colour, size, density). That's a mode.
3. Never make a token used once, or one that equals another token in every mode.
4. Never put a mode on a container just to change its background. Use a direct fill. (Use a mode when the things on it *should* change too, like text going white on dark.)
5. Never wrap a component in another just to add one style layer.
6. Never detach to tweak. Rebase on purpose and give it a name.

**Judgment calls, not absolutes:** fixed layers vs a slot for semi-structured content; variants vs separate masters; a separate Pad collection.
add.title: Absolutes: always and never

add.text:
**If the content is one-off, use the slot. If the arrangement repeats, make it a master.**

- A Card with a `Content` slot can hold anything, so for one-off cards you **never need to rebase**. Drop things in and you're done.
- The moment the same arrangement appears a second time, you'd be copying a hand-edited slot, which is where our hundreds of untemplated cards came from. Two ways to make it a master:
  - **B, rebase:** detach the Card, make it `Card · Newsletter`, and re-make the slot. Flat (one layer fewer), but it forks the shell: later changes to the base Card's structure don't reach it. Its values still do, through tokens.
  - **D, content master in the slot:** keep the generic Card shell, make `Newsletter content` a master, and drop one instance of it into the slot. The shell stays linked *and* the content is templated, at the cost of one extra layer to click through.
- The test that settles B vs D is running now; the verdict lands here.
add.title: Slot or rebase? One line decides it

add.text:
1. **Tokens.** Colors (palette), Scheme (White / Light gray / Prime / Dark), Scale (the 4-width plan), Button, Selection, Icon size, and maybe Pad. Plus 8 text styles and 1 effect style, `Card shadow`.
2. **Elements**, the things you place: Icon (with the visual glyph picker), Button, Icon button, Pill, Icon item, the Inputs, Media (image). Text is just a text layer with a style; it's not a component.
3. **Containers**, things that hold other things. Each name tells you the padding:
   - **Section:** a flush band, no padding of its own, optional background, can nest.
   - **Card:** a padded content slot with the card edge (radius token + `Card shadow`; clip only when media needs the corners).
   - **Panel system:** not one component but a *named family* of stackable parts that share a look (header, rows, footer) and work well together in a stack. A plain unpadded wrapper doesn't need to be a component; that's just a Section.
4. **Layouts:** grids are plain frames with the gap token (no grid components), plus `.Masonry` and the Page template.

Purpose-built cards (Newsletter, Stat, Avatar…) sit on their family page, made by B or D above. That's about 11 core components, not 220.
add.title: The core kit, organized in four tiers

add.text:
Estimates for our kit. Fewer steps is the goal.

| Task | Tool | Steps |
|---|---|---|
| Drop a card with my own text | instance | drag, type |
| 3 identical cards in a row | inline master + copies | Ctrl+D twice |
| A card with the image on the left | variant, *if* a `Card Set` has Media = Top / Left | 1 dropdown (rebase: about 5 steps) |
| Change every card's radius | token | 1 edit |
| A dark section | Scheme mode on the section | 1 click |
| A different icon | swap, visual picker | 1 click + pick |
| A new card type used in 3 places | rebase (or D) once, then copies | about 5 steps once, then Ctrl+D |
| Make one card not follow the section's mode | its own mode | 1 click |

The design rule this suggests: **the common jobs should be 1 or 2 steps.** If a common job takes 5, that's the missing master or variant.
add.title: Designer experience: steps per everyday task

add.text:
- **Modes cascade** to every child that has no mode of its own. To opt a child out, give it its own mode.
- **One mode per collection per frame**, so independent switches need separate collections. The Pad test showed Scale = SM plus Pad = None works, at the cost of one more switch.
- **Variants don't inherit from each other.** Each one is a full copy.
- **Editing one item in a slot overrides the whole slot** (forum report; testing now). **Reset** brings it back, and throws away the edits.
- **Properties can't bind to layers inside a slot** (Figma docs). Use variables or modes there.
- **Detaching turns slots into plain frames.** Re-make them as slots.
- **Resizing a copy makes a size override.** It stops following the master's size until you reset it.
- **These can't be tokens:** layout direction, layer order, nesting, clip content, grid column count.
- **Across files:** library variables are read-only, and there's no child design system that inherits. Duplicating a file makes independent copies. Extended collections (Enterprise) are the only real override.
- **Preferred values only suggest** for swaps and slots. Any component can still be picked by search.
add.title: Every caveat in one place
Where the file is now (counted tonight)

3. **Approve the Scale plan** (4 widths) and decide on Pad as its own collection.
4. **Retire the collections** listed above.
5. **Name the containers:** Section, Card and the Panel system, as on this page.
6. **Write the absolutes** into the Figma readme, so every agent builds this way.

add.title: How we get from here to there

add.text:
- [Nathan Curtis, Configuration collapse](https://nathanacurtis.substack.com/p/configuration-collapse): "Make the common configurable, make the uncommon composable." The core Card becomes an unopinionated container, and purpose cards (ProductCard) wrap it.
- [Figma help: slots](https://help.figma.com/hc/en-us/articles/38231200344599): slot structure is locked on instances, *reset* goes back to the master, properties can't bind inside slots, and preferred instances only guide.
- [Figma forum: overriding one item marks the whole slot overridden](https://forum.figma.com/suggest-a-feature-11/overriding-one-element-inside-a-slot-marks-the-entire-slot-as-overridden-51686/index2.html)
- [Figma forum: nested slots break variant switching once overridden](https://forum.figma.com/report-a-problem-6/nested-slots-break-variant-switching-once-slot-content-is-overridden-56034)
- Our tests: the Card strategy page (477:44553), the Grids page (464:10330), and the Claude November 2026 notes pages.
add.title: Sources

fc-slot-rebase.text:
**One-off content: put loose layers in the slot. Content that repeats: make it a master and put one instance of it in the slot.**

Tested tonight on the Card strategy page (shell `491:10452`, content master `491:10451`):

| Change | B, rebase (detach, new master) | D, shell + content master in the slot |
|---|---|---|
| Reorder or add a layer in the template | all follow | all follow |
| Change the base shell's padding | **no**, stays 48 | **yes** |
| Radius token | follows | follows |
| Per-card text survives | yes | yes |
| Title depth / layers | 3 / 7 | 4 / 8 |
| Ctrl-click to edit the title | 1 click | 1 click |

- **The forum claim is half true.** Edit *loose* layers inside a slot and the copy owns that slot, so later master changes stop (confirmed on A). Edit text inside an *instance* that sits in the slot and only that text is overridden, and the slot keeps following (the slot gap change reached all 3 D cards).
- **Verdict: D.** One generic Card shell, plus purpose content masters (`Newsletter content`, `Stat content`…) dropped into its slot. Everything follows, and Ctrl-click makes the extra layer cost nothing.
- **New absolute:** *never repeat loose layers in a slot; repeat an instance.*
fc-slot-rebase.title: Slot or rebase? Answered: fill the slot with an instance

add.text:
**Three levels:**
1. **An instance:** the default. When you're designing, always place instances of what exists, and only type over text and images.
2. **A local master,** in the file you're designing in: the *second* time an arrangement repeats, the first one becomes the master (inline master). It doesn't go in the library yet.
3. **A library master:** promote it only when it's (a) used in 2 or more files, or one of the core tiers, (b) approved by screenshot, and (c) not already covered by an existing master or by a content master in the Card's slot.

**A budget keeps the library small:** about 7 collections, about 12 core components and about 10 content masters. Adding one means retiring one, or saying why not.

**Fewer pages: split the file.** The design system file has 47 pages. Suggested split:
- **Lew42 Design System (the library), ~12 pages:** Start here, Tokens (plus one ↳ page per collection), Text, Icons, Elements, Containers, Content masters, Layouts.
- **Lew42 Lab (explorations):** Live, Grids, Card strategy, Flow, the resolution pages, Text layouts, Explore · Masonry, Component notes, Walkthroughs, Sandbox, Devices, Docs, Workspace, Approval workflows.
- **Apps** (Tasks, Chat, Editor) live in their own project files and *use* the library.
- **The Cut list** goes to an archive file.

**Caveat:** pages can't be moved between files by script, so it's copy and paste by hand. Pasted *instances* stay linked to the published library, but pasted *masters* become new, separate masters. So masters that are reused (like the Flow kit) stay in the library, or get promoted before the move.
add.title: When something earns a master, and when it goes in the library

Full table: `ext/Figma/doc/token-audit.md`. Live demos: the ↳ Colors, ↳ Scheme and ↳ Scale pages.

**Keep (9), renamed "Lew42 · …":** Colors, Scheme, Scale, Constants, Button, Selection, Icon size, Image, Bar.

**Merge (3):**
- `Card padding` into Scale. The Card binds Scale padding directly; Panel gets 0.
- `Theme` into Scheme. Accent aliases Colors prime; Blue, Gold and Teal go to the Cut list.

**Scale flags,** visible side by side on ↳ Scale (no values changed):
- **XS and Mobile** are nearly the same (pad-x 16 / 16, h1 32 / 32). Merge candidate.
- **Mega is smaller than XL** in padding and buttons (pad-x 56 vs 80, btn-pad-x 24 vs 40). The ladder isn't in order.
- **gap-y** equals gap everywhere except Mobile. Drop candidate.
- **Radius** is 3 to 4 in four of the seven modes, hard to tell apart.
- **Icon size:** Body and Label are both 16.
- **Desktop (1920)** has no mode of its own; it uses Default.

add.text:
One master layout with 8 copies from 360 to 3440, each changing only its width plus the Scale mode on its `Layout` frame ([the row](https://www.figma.com/design/hbolzQ3Xnc78rhxAPj8xK2?node-id=513-10742)).

**Can one master scale from 3440 down to 360? Yes, with two swaps per size: the menu bar and the grid's column count.**

| Pattern | Verdict |
|---|---|
| Two-column split (wrap, both sides fill, min 280) | works: stacks below about 580 |
| Flex wrap cards (fill, min 280, max 400) | works with caveats: reflows from 1 to 6 columns, but the max leaves mixed sizes and gaps |
| Grid with fixed columns | needs a swap: never reflows; a copy ignores a new column count, so swap a `Grid Set` |
| Menu bar | needs a swap: `Nav Set` Compact (logo + menu button), picked by hand per size |
| Small layout nested in a card | works by itself |

**The wrap recipe that works:** horizontal, wrap on, the container at a fixed width, cards set to fill with a min width (320). Cards must sit directly in the wrap frame; set Fill after adding them.

Add a max width only to stop a lone last card from stretching. Figma has no "below 600, use Compact" rule, so every per-size swap is manual.
add.title: Live responsive previews: what works

add.text:
**The problem:** a mode switches *every* value in its collection on that layer and everything inside it. To change only the padding, a Scale mode also changes the gap, radius and squeeze.

**Options:**
1. **One Scale collection.** Simplest. Fine when "make this whole thing smaller" is what you want.
2. **Separate Pad collection with size modes.** Lets padding switch on its own. Costs one more switch per frame (tested: works).
3. **Fixed named padding tokens** (pad-sm, pad-md, pad-lg) in a one-mode collection, bound **directly** on the layer. No modes at all, so nothing cascades.

**Leaning:** 1 + 3. Scale modes resize a whole card or section; a named padding token handles a one-off. Not decided; nothing built.

**v2 file:** `Lew42 v2 · Scale` with only pad-x, pad-y, gap, radius and squeeze (was content-max).
